title: Contextual onboarding and org-policy aware admin-access routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise customers submit a wide range of admin and org-access requests (RBAC changes, SSO/SAML enablement, SCIM provisioning, org policy exceptions). The current intake form results in manual triage, long SLAs, and routing to the wrong team. Goal: build a contextual intake workflow that scores requests automatically, enriches them with org metadata, surfaces SLO recommendations, and routes to the correct resolver (support L2, IAM ops, account engineering, or security).
proposed_flow: 1) Customer fills intake form with minimal required fields. 2) Enrichment step pulls org manifest (tenant tier, current SSO/SCIM status, existing RBAC roles) and recent support incidents. 3) Scoring engine computes risk/priority using weighted signals (customer tier, sensitive roles requested, presence of existing SSO, audit-log gaps). 4) Recommend SLA and default assignee queue; provide suggested remediation steps and a templated SCIM payload when applicable. 5) Allow human override and feedback to retrain scorer.
acceptance_criteria: - Intake form added to console and support portal with required fields and metadata enrichment. - Automated enrichments return tenant tier and SSO status >= 95% for test tenants. - Scoring engine produces priority labels (low/med/high/urgent) with >= 85% match to historical manual triage on sample set. - Routing rules forward >90% of high/urgent to security or IAM ops accurately during pilot. - UX shows suggested remediation and a one-click template for common SCIM/SAML tasks.
ux_notes: Form should surface contextual help based on request type (e.g., when RBAC change -> show role sensitivity matrix). Add checkbox for 'makes production-facing changes' to set high priority. Inline links to relevant tenant audit logs and org policy docs. Design to support both support ticket and console entry points.
scoring_weights: Suggested default weights: customer_tier=0.35; sensitive_role=0.25; recent_incidents=0.20; sso_missing=0.10; explicit_high_risk_flag=0.10. Thresholds: urgent>=0.8; high>=0.6; medium>=0.35; low<0.35.
data_requirements: Enrichment API must return: tenant_id, plan_tier, current_sso_state, scim_enabled, list_of_recent_incidents (ids), last_audit_log_timestamp. Acceptable fallback: manual upload or link to support ticket when API unavailable.
implementation_notes: Epic split across frontend (console & support portal), backend enrichments service (ENG-4022), scoring microservice, and routing configuration in ops. Use feature flag rollout (console-intake-v1). Add telemetry events for every triage decision.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: false positives route sensitive requests incorrectly -> Mitigation: start with conservative thresholds and require human approval for urgent auto-assign. Risk: data availability for enrichment -> Mitigation: graceful fallback to manual fields and mark 'enrichment missing' in UI.
privacy_and_compliance: Ensure enrichment requests are authorized by tenant consent. Log minimal identifiers only. SCIM payloads must be exposed to resolver queues only with RBAC gating. Coordinate with Security for KMS/HSM requirements if storing tokens.
next_steps: 1) PM to finalize intake fields and labels (due 2026-03-12). 2) Design to deliver mockups (Marco) by 2026-03-18. 3) ENG to estimate backend work (ENG-4022) and begin prototyping scoring service. 4) Pilot with three customers in Cycle 2026-W12.
